doc.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023

title: Recording 'Healing Time' live with her band
summary: Recorded largely live in New Orleans with her band and producer Mark Howard; first album written with the band, honoring drummer Samantha Banks.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you record — this may change from one CD to the next — but do you mostly record live with your band?

Yeah, you know actually I don’t — this last CD that I did, “Healing Time” is recorded with my band and we did record live for the most part. Yeah. Come to think of it, as far as the rhythm section yeah, we definitely did play live for “Healing Time.” And looking back I played live for the most part on most of my recordings, but not all. And I used studio musicians up until now and the last CD, “Healing Time,” is actually my band for the most part and I had a group of guys that, a wonderful group of guys in New Orleans that were produced by Mark Howard. We played live in the same room, honestly. There were no, you know, in the control booth. And that was fun. Yeah.
Yeah I listened to “Healing Time” and there’s a phrase not so much anymore but, “Wow that jumps off the record.” And that tune jumps off the record. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

It’s like, and it sounds like there was more arranging to be done with some horn parts and a choir and so forth. Was there a discussion about this next CD is going to sound somewhat different from what came before it?

I think it was unconsciously done that way. We — I did want to write with my band on this one. This was the first album we’ve actually written together and that was huge for me because I had — we had just come out of the pandemic, just that January, out of the pandemic and started recording. And not even just recording but writing. We were recording and writing about the same time as much as we could. And I wanted to honor, I really wanted to honor my drummer and friend Samantha Banks. She passed away in ’19, in 2019 of a stroke and that really, it took a lot out of all of us. And I wanted to honor her memory and her musicianship by bringing the band in for this next project and record and perform and write as a family, as my band family. And I’ve got to say it just kind of happened. I think the reason this record, and I’m proud of all of my albums, but this one really is special to me mostly because I’m close to it and you know it’s just out, but because my band is on there and there’s so much love and respect and sweat and hours of recording and re-recording and sequencing the songs so that they sound great together coming in and out of each other. And then working on the songs so that we can perform them live especially after all of the arranging that you noticed has to be — all of that was added after we did the basic, the base part. That’s huge for me. A lot went into this album and a lot of my own money went into this own album. So yeah I’m really close to this one. And I know they’re real proud of it too. I’ve watched and I read interviews that they’re doing about their own songs. All of my band members have their own careers and play with other bands and their own bands. So they know what goes into making a record from writing, from concept to playing it on stage. And that’s why I really respect them all for that. They know how much work goes into that. And because of that we’re all real proud of this album, “Healing Time.”
